# River-valley background

Generated with the built-in image-generation tool, using the user's `hllv-image-inspiration.jpg` as a mood/subject reference. This is decorative generated scenery, not an official game screenshot or historical photograph. The supplied reference is not modified or redistributed in the site.

Production assets:
- `hllv_tracker/assets/river-valley-10064d0556445fad.webp` — 1942 × 809, 130842 bytes.
- `hllv_tracker/assets/river-valley-mobile-2019c320c527506a.webp` — 960 px wide, 39116 bytes.

The generated PNG was format-optimized into WebP without creative edits. The original remains in the generated-image output. Native `picture` selection loads the smaller asset on phones. The image is decorative (`alt=""`, `aria-hidden="true"`), does not change layout, and never intercepts input. CSS scrims preserve legibility and fade the image before the record lists. The older map treatment remains only as a faint edge layer. If imagery cannot load, the existing solid theme remains usable.

## Final generation prompt

Use case: historical-scene.
Asset type: wide photographic website background for a Hell Let Loose: Vietnam community tracker; an original atmospheric scene, NOT a website mockup and NOT an official game screenshot.
Input image 1 is a mood/subject reference only. Borrow its humid river valley, jungle canopy, muted olive and blue-green haze, and recognizably Vietnam-era Huey helicopter. Do not recreate its exact camera position, foreground gun, watermark, or composition.
Create a naturalistic, understated 1960s Vietnam river-valley aerial photograph. A broad winding river cuts diagonally through irregular jungle canopy and low distant ridges, with layered humid haze. One realistic UH-1 Huey seen at medium distance in the upper-right portion, not huge, with correct single two-bladed main rotor, tail boom and tail rotor, cockpit and landing skids. A second tiny distant helicopter is optional only if composition requires it. No foreground people, gun, muzzle flashes, tracer fire, explosions or dramatic orange lighting.
Composition: very wide 2.4:1 landscape, approximately 2400 by 1000. This background sits behind live HTML text. Left 45 percent must be quieter, lower contrast and shadowed with broad atmospheric shapes. Aircraft and river detail concentrated right, with enough surrounding air and vegetation to remain convincing when cropped. Natural asymmetry. River should be readable but not glowing. Distant horizon no higher than upper quarter. Bottom edge becomes softly shadowed jungle; no hard vignette.
Style: weathered editorial documentary color photography, believable landscape and optics, fine subtle film grain, muted grey-green foliage, warm worn olive metal, subdued teal-grey water, soft overcast light. Tactile and restrained rather than synthetic polish or cinematic key art. No plastic surfaces, ornate repeated patterns, oversharpening, glossy HDR, lens flares, excessive fog, giant sun or perfect radial gradients.
Do not draw contour lines into this image; a separate restrained cartographic layer will be added in CSS. No text, lettering, branding, UI, borders or watermark. Do not use transparency.
